skills.name: editable-export
skills.description: Give the person an editable copy of a video you made, built from its elements (footage clips, text, graphics, sounds, music), which opens in the EditAtlas studio, a web page with a timeline. There they fix small things themselves and export the MP4 again in their browser, without asking you to edit and re-render. Typical fixes are a sound a little late or too loud, text slightly off, captions too small, a typo, a clip a few frames long. The copy is a folder on their computer (kept in Google Drive from the studio, it also gets a link). Each save adds a version, so you can take turns. It is optional. Offer it when you deliver a video, and build it only when they want it. Also use it when someone asks for "an editable version", "a project file", to "tweak it myself", pastes a message from EditAtlas Studio, "chỉnh lại chút", "tự sửa", "file để sửa", "chỉnh cỡ chữ", or "âm thanh bị trễ" after an edit. It is not a full editor; effects burned into the clips cannot be changed there.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ and FFmpeg with ffprobe. render.py needs Playwright (pip install playwright), Chrome or Edge, and network access to edit.trysometh.ing to load the studio page; the files stay on the machine. share.py (reading and adding to a link the person gives you) needs the cryptography package and network access. The person needs Chrome or Edge 94+ (WebCodecs, and saving into a folder); Safari and Firefox are not tested. Works with the transcribe and sound-design skills.

skills.name: media-picker
skills.description: Find, pick and place B-roll (stock clips for the lines of a voice-over), background music, photos and sound effects that fit the video, and check each before it goes into the edit. Use it before calling search_videos, search_music, search_photos or search_sfx, or downloading from Pexels or Pixabay, whenever a video needs B-roll, cutaway shots or music, when B-roll goes on the words of a voice-over or talking head, and when someone says a pick does not fit. Measures candidates (shake, cuts, crop; music tempo, intro, energy), looks at every frame sheet, has the person hear music options, and places clips on their words, colour-matched, off the face. Triggers include "cần B-roll cho mấy câu này", "chèn B-roll vào video", "tìm cảnh trên Pexels", "tìm b-roll", "tìm nhạc nền", "chọn nhạc nền", "nhạc nền không hay", "cảnh bị rung", "find B-roll for these lines", "add B-roll to this voice-over", "find background music". Not for checking a finished render (video-check) or placing sounds on frames (sound-design).
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy and Pillow, and FFmpeg with ffprobe. Needs network access to download candidates, or the files downloaded by the person. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell that can read images.

skills.name: sound-design
skills.description: Sound-design a finished video with real sound effects from the EditAtlas library (2,278 described sounds, public, downloadable from GitHub with SHA-256 checks). Finds the moments in the picture, lets you look at them as frame sheets, picks sounds by description and measured numbers, places each on its exact frame at a level set by its role, keeps or replaces the film's own music and voice, renders a new MP4 plus a separate SFX WAV, and checks the result in numbers (sync, pace, holes, loudness, mono) before you show it. Use it whenever someone asks to add sound effects, SFX, whooshes, pops, clicks, hits, UI sounds or "sound design" to a video, reel, short, promo, motion graphic, product demo or talking-head edit; says a video "feels silent", "needs sound", "thêm hiệu ứng âm thanh", "lồng SFX", "thêm tiếng động"; or wants EditAtlas sounds placed on a video rather than just found. Not for composing music or generating sound.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy and Pillow, FFmpeg with ffprobe, and network access to raw.githubusercontent.com (or a local clone of EditAtlas/sfx). Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell.

skills.name: talking-head-cut
skills.description: Cut a raw talking-head recording (one person speaking to camera, a lesson, a vlog, a voice-over take) into a clean video. Takes out false starts, failed and repeated takes, words said to the editor ("take two", "nói lại nhé"), doubled words and um/uh/ờ/ừm, and shortens long pauses to a breath, also with music or noise under the voice. When the script was recorded several times across files, picks the best take of each line. You quote the words; the scripts find them, put every cut in silence, render picture and sound in step, then transcribe the cut again to catch leftovers and clipped words. Use it for "cut my mistakes out", "clean up this take", "remove the retakes", "pick the best takes", "cắt video nói chuyện", "cắt chỗ nói hỏng", "bỏ đoạn nói lại", "chọn take tốt nhất", "cắt ờ ừm và khoảng lặng". Needs the transcribe skill's word-level transcript. Not for subtitles alone (transcribe), highlights from a long video, multi-camera edits, or adding music, B-roll or captions (after the cut).
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy, FFmpeg with ffprobe, and the EditAtlas transcribe skill (faster-whisper) for the transcript and for verify.py. Runs on the person's machine; nothing is uploaded. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell.

skills.name: transcribe
skills.description: Transcribe the speech in a video or audio file on the person's own machine with Whisper (faster-whisper), with a time for every word, then check it, write SRT/VTT subtitles, and list what an edit could cut (long silences, filler words like um, uh, ờ, ừm, and repeated takes). The checked word-level transcript is what EditAtlas caption techniques, silence and filler removal, retake selection and every template's verified_transcript input need. Use it whenever someone wants a transcript, subtitles, captions or an SRT from a video; asks to "trích lời", "lấy lời thoại", "chuyển giọng nói thành chữ", "làm phụ đề", "làm sub", "cắt khoảng lặng", "bỏ ờ ừm", "speech to text", "Whisper"; or starts an EditAtlas edit that needs word times, even if they never say "transcript". Installs Whisper only after asking. Not for translating, cleaning up audio, separating a voice from music, or making a voice.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with faster-whisper (pip, about 300 MB on disk) and FFmpeg with ffprobe. The first run downloads a Whisper model from Hugging Face (0.5 to 1.6 GB); after that it works offline and no audio leaves the machine. For English, an optional 95 MB alignment model (Apache-2.0, run by the onnxruntime that faster-whisper installs, no torch) sharpens word times. Runs on CPU; an NVIDIA GPU is faster. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell.

skills.name: video-breakdown
skills.description: Break down a reference video shot by shot and name what it does, so the person can make one like it. Measures cuts and transitions (dissolve, dip, wipe, shape, iris, push, zoom, flash), camera moves (crash zoom, push in, shake, speed change), text and graphics and their timing (in, hold, out, stagger), text colours, gradients, backgrounds, font size and free lookalike fonts, the look, pacing, the beat and sound hits; you look at the frames, look up each element in EditAtlas and write a report with technique names, sounds and a recipe. Use it when someone shares a video they like and asks what effect, transition or edit is in it, how it was made, or how to remake it; says "video này dùng hiệu ứng gì", "phân tích video mẫu", "làm sao để edit giống video này", "hiệu ứng chuyển cảnh này tên gì", "what transition is this"; or asks why their remake does not look like the reference ("so sánh bản làm lại"). Works on a local file. Not for downloading from TikTok or YouTube, telling filmed from AI footage, or editing.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy and Pillow, and FFmpeg with ffprobe. Runs offline; only the optional --check-api step, font lookalikes (downloaded once from Google Fonts) and the EditAtlas MCP use the network. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell that can read images.

skills.name: video-check
skills.description: Check a finished video before the person sees it or posts it, then fix what is wrong. Measures the file (size, frame rate, pixel format, length), picture faults (black or white frames, frozen stretches, one-frame glitches and wrong frames at cuts, stutter, loop seams), sound (loudness, clipping, silences, abrupt ends) and text too small or too brief for a phone; makes frame sheets at phone size and a strip around each cut; a reviewer who has not seen your plan judges them by the kind of video (tutorial, talking head, ad, reel, film) and, from round 2, checks each claimed fix on the new frames. Fix the worst three, render again, at most three rounds. Use it after rendering any edit, and when someone asks to check a video before sending or posting it, says "kiểm tra video trước khi gửi", "xem lại bản dựng", "video này có lỗi gì không", "review my edit", "QA this render". Works on a local file. Not for breaking down someone else's video (use video-breakdown) or for judging footage the person has not edited.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy and Pillow, and FFmpeg with ffprobe. Runs offline. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell that can read images; a reviewer subagent is used when the agent can start one.
